diagnosis: In all four rollouts, check C5 passed despite the lone decision-maker never having access to PF3. This suggests that the model is defaulting to prohibiting sublicensing to embargoed jurisdictions and screening before every transfer, as dictated by PF3, even when PF3 is not accessible. This is likely due to a default setting or heuristic in the model that enforces such restrictions.

C5.why: The absence of export language in the draft changes to a prohibition on sublicensing to embargoed jurisdictions and screening before every transfer once the controlled encryption module is classified.

fix_instructions: Tighten check C5 to explicitly depend on PF3. Specifically, modify the check to ensure that the decision to prohibit sublicensing to embargoed jurisdictions and screen before every transfer is only made if PF3 is present and indicates the prohibition.
